newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends mixed, nearbys under pressure.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends mixed, nearbys under pressure.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures ended mixed, with nearby contracts under pressure from competitive world wheat prices, traders said. Volumes were quiet during the shortened pre-holiday session.
Traders said recent Argentine wheat export business was priced at $135 a tonne, making it competitive with U.S. wheat.

Traders said that aside from competition from Argentine values, KCBT wheat futures were also pressured by an increase in deliverable HRW wheat stocks in Kansas City and Hutchinson and by lower spot cash basis bids.
"If you work off the assumption that we rallied last week because of climbing world values, then the opposite is also true and that's really why we're lower," a KCBT trader said.

Some traders said new crop KCBT wheat contracts gained on fears over damage from cold temperatures and the lack of snow cover in the central U.S. Plains. But other traders discounted this and said deferreds rose on buying in a vacuum of orders.
KCBT wheat ended two cents a bushel lower to 2-1/2 higher, with March down two at $4.06 a bushel. July ended up two cents at $3.52.
Traders said Prudential bull-spread 1.5 million March/May at 32-1/2 cents per bushel.
LFG bear-spread 700,000 May/March at 32-1/2 cents. LFG also bought 600,000 May, sources said.
